note: Relays for GitHub release downloads, used by the in-app updater when the
release origin itself can't be reached — see src-tauri/src/github_mirror.rs.
This file has two roles and is one source of truth for both: it is compiled
into the app as the default list (include_str!), and the copy of it on `main`
is what installed clients re-read over jsDelivr. So editing it here and
merging re-points every client that is already out there, without shipping a
release — which matters because a broken update path is exactly the situation
where an update can't carry the fix. jsDelivr caches a branch path for about
12 hours, so allow that long to propagate.
Rules the client enforces on whatever it reads (see parse_mirror_list):
- https only, and a host that parses; anything else is dropped
- order is the order they're tried, after the origin
- a list that ends up empty is refused, and the previous one stays in force
Only *relays* live here. The release origin is compiled in separately and is
always tried first, so nothing in this file can redirect the primary route,
and every download is verified against the app's minisign pubkey regardless.
Each host takes a whole GitHub URL appended to it:
https://<host>/https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/...
A candidate has to follow the redirect to release-assets.githubusercontent.com
server-side and honour Range, or resuming breaks. Verified 2026-09-06 against
v0.12.1: byte-identical sha256 over the full 35 MB .exe, no size cap at 70 MB,
206 with a Content-Range naming the total.
